description: Prefer this over freehand set_script. Rotate one body of the active part by angle degrees (right-hand rule) about the line through center along axis: the Rotate button, directly below Move. axis is x, y, or z (a leading - flips it) or an [ax, ay, az] vector; center is [x, y, z] in mm, or omitted for the body's own centroid; angle defaults to 90. Name the body the same way as insert_move: body_index or at from list_bodies, face or face_id from list_faces, or use_selection with a selected face. Nothing named and nothing selected is no_body; the origin is never assumed. Volume is unchanged and the bounding box follows the turn. edit_feature on the rotate takes angle, axis, center, and at. Working copy only; git_save commits. Build in ribbon order: block out every part of the assembly as plain blocks first (within seconds of the prompt, then screenshot for the user), then Build and Shape, then Polish, then pattern and place; finish each stage across the whole assembly before the next. Features first: insert_code_snippet { gap, why, script } is the fallback for one operation no feature can do (its block starts with // FEATURE-GAP: <missing feature or option> | <why the existing feature did not work>); set_script only rewrites a whole part. Hardware is one part per unique fastener type, one instance patterned to every place it goes. Fix one base part with a fixed joint, then place every part that touches or attaches to another with joint_create (one call creates the joint and solves placement). Use part_set_transform only for parts that touch nothing. Block-out positions are rough; joints set final positions. If the geometry engine crashes under this part (out of memory, a wasm abort, or a run past its 30 s budget) the result is ok: false with crash { code: geometry_worker_crashed, reason: wasm_abort | out_of_memory | timeout | worker_lost, workerRestarted: true } and one failures row with the same code; status.runState is failed. The worker was already replaced and other parts kept building, so do not ask for a reload and do not retry the same script: simplify the part, lower segment counts, or split it into smaller parts, then run it again. When the run past the budget was inside one marked feature block, the part is rebuilt without that block instead: the result is ok: false with one failures row { code: feature_timeout, featureId, featureType, featureLabel, elapsedMs, budgetMs, detail }, status.runState is failed, the other features are built and shown, and status.featureMs (and feature_tree ms) say how long each block took; edit, delete, or undo that feature. Writes (defaults): rotateAbout(manifold, axis, angleDeg, center, { bodies }) — turn one body about an axis through a point Takes return: "status" | "summary" | "full" (MCP default "status": status.script is omitted; "summary" adds status.features; "full" echoes the script).

at.description: Body centroid [x, y, z] mm from list_bodies

axis.description: 'x', 'y', or 'z' (a leading '-' flips it), or an [ax, ay, az] vector; right-hand rule

center.description: [x, y, z] in mm; omit or null for the default

face.description: A list_faces key { at, n, area } on the body to rotate

face_id.description: A list_faces id (f12) on the body to rotate

return.description: How much of status to return: "status" drops status.script, "summary" drops it and adds status.features (the feature strip), "full" keeps the whole script. Over MCP the default is "status"; in the page it is "full". Read the script with get_script.

use_selection.description: When true and no body_index, at, face_id, or face is given, rotate the body of the selected face

name: insert_rotate
